title: Book One · Chapter 151: A Smaller Story
story:
At break a boy from another class looks at the stool card. He has come to borrow chalk from Miss Wu. The card is on Ronan's desk beside the room plan.

“Your show has an old chair?” he asks.

“A stool.”

“Do you have anything new?”

Ronan closes his hand over the edge of the card. He wants to say they have many new things. He wants to tell the boy about the shop. He wants to explain the move. Dad can still work well. He wants the boy to know that too. He wants to tell the boy all of it. He holds the card tightly, ready to speak.

Mei looks up from her picture. “The drawings are new.”

The boy looks at them. He points to one window. “Which street is this?” he asks. Mei tells him. He borrows the chalk and leaves. He leaves before Ronan can say anything more. He only asked about the old stool and new things.

Still, Ronan is cross. He puts the card inside his book so no one else can look. Leo comes over. “Where will we put the game?” he asks. Ronan answers in an angry voice.

“I only asked about a table,” Leo says.

Ronan looks at him. “Sorry.”

He explains about the boy. Leo sits on the edge of the next chair.

“It is old,” he says.

“I know.”

“So is Mr Qiu's box.”

“I know that too.”

Leo taps the room plan. “They are things people use. You wanted to show useful things.”

Ronan takes the card out again. The words have not changed. The boy did not say “poor” or “bad.” Ronan thought he meant those things. But he did not actually say them.

He opens the card one more time. Then he starts packing his bag. His hand pressed the edge. A little mark is there now. He smooths it against the desk. Leo helps him put it between two clean pages. Neither boy says more about the other child. The boy asked a question and then left. Ronan can leave him alone now.

After school he tells Mum about the boy. He repeats the boy's words. She is cutting cloth at the table. She moves the sharp scissors away before she turns to listen.

“Do you want to change the display?” she asks.

“I want it to be good.”

“Then we should make the good parts clear.”

She picks up her blue bag. The cloth is plain and did not cost much. The edges are neat. The handles feel soft and wide in his hand. He lifts it with a few schoolbooks inside. It hangs evenly.

“This is good,” he says.

“Show them the good handles.”

He writes a new question for the bag card: WHAT MAKES A BAG EASY TO CARRY? He can say Mum works hard. But this question helps visitors look at the bag itself. They can try the handles and feel the soft cloth.

Then he reads Dad's card. ONE LEG WAS LOOSE. DAD REPAIRED IT. There is something visitors can see there too. The leg was loose before. Now people can sit safely on it. Visitors can see the repaired leg.

That night he sits on it while Mum checks his reading. He gets one hard word wrong twice. She covers the second half with her finger and helps him read the first. He tries again.

When he gets it, Dad calls from the doorway, “A new word on an old stool.”

Ronan laughs. He likes Dad's joke. He is glad he can read the new word. He is also glad the old stool is safe again.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：cross＝生气的；evenly＝均匀平稳地；neat＝整齐的。

情节提示：scissors＝剪刀；handles＝提手；stool＝凳子。

理解：1. 另一班男孩的话为什么让 Ronan 难受？2. Mum 建议怎样向别人展示袋子的好处？
